topic_title: Speed Related to Stopping & Roadway Conditions
prompt: When a vehicle's cruising speed doubles from 30 mph to 60 mph, how does its braking distance change?

options.text: Braking distance increases by four times because energy quadruples with speed
Braking distance doubles in direct proportion to the increase in road speed
Braking distance triples due to moderate mechanical heating of brake shoes
Braking distance remains identical provided the antilock brakes operate
